chunk_map.heading: Great research can still miss the outcome

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: line 8: "Those snapshots are what your agents read next." closest to violating; "snapshots" resolves to "one-page snapshot" in the same sentence-pair; "her" (lines 4, 6, 8) resolves to Teresa Torres named in line 4; "your agents" is the training's own frame, not a slide referent.
grep for 'lecture|module|earlier|previous|opening' in body_numbered -> 0; line 8 "Those snapshots are what your agents read next" points forward in reading order, not at a file by position.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.evidence: no 'the X you did/saw/caught' construction; closest is line 4 "Teresa Torres often sees teams", a report about others, not a room beat.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.na_reason: no guess/predict or demo beat on the slide

rules_evaluated.evidence: line 4: "Teresa Torres often sees teams who are great at research and still don't meet their outcomes." is a self-carrying claim; slide has three paragraphs.
header "Great research can still miss the outcome" (line 1) is what line 4 states and what lines 6 and 8 remedy; nothing in the body contradicts it.

none of the six sub-items present: no 'Not X. Not Y. Z.'; no anaphora triple; no self-grading superlative (line 4 "great at research" describes teams, quoted-paraphrase of Torres); no number + retraction; no abstraction-noun stack ("in service of a desired outcome" is a verbatim Torres quote, line 4); no verb triplet. Closest: line 6 four-part list, which is a verbed sentence naming her definition, not a tic.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
rules_evaluated.evidence: body words checked: snapshot, research activities, desired product outcome, agents are ordinary product/engineering vocabulary; no surface-as-noun, compendium, beat, mood, firing. Maintainer-block 'Fidelity guard' vocabulary is not on the slide.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -c '\*\*' on body.txt -> 0; no bold in the body.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Presence precedes content — verify against the composed deck, not long-read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: lecture apt101-go-back-to-your-customers.md includes it as a standalone-paragraph slide-file link at its line 5 ('[Great research can still miss the outcome](slides/talk-to-customers-every-week.md)'), the transparent-include shape that reaches the deck; slide file carries its own ## and <!--slide:--> id.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Numbering — position is computed, content ordinals are linted.
rules_evaluated.evidence: node scripts/check-slide-numbering.js --file curriculum/slides/talk-to-customers-every-week.md -> OK, Phase/Step numbering consistent; no hand-numbered header.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Page geometry dies at the cut; reading order survives.
rules_evaluated.evidence: node scripts/check-slide-deixis.js --file ... -> OK, no page-geometry pointers across the slide cut; grep below|above|see below in body -> 0.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: In-deck links work now; whether they EARN their place is open.
rules_evaluated.na_reason: no in-body links on the slide (grep '](' on body.txt -> 0); rule is a review aid, never a gate

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Slide size — 210 words / 6 bullets, and the cap is machine-checked.
rules_evaluated.evidence: node scripts/check-slide-size.js --file ... -> files: 1 slides: 1, oversized: 0, every slide within limits.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: lecture heading "Great research can still miss the outcome" (line 1) is a claim, as lecture headings are required to be; lecture, not exercise.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A bullet earns its slot or dies — three classes that read as rigour and carry nothing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: line 8 "Those snapshots are what your agents read next." is the closest to a kicker, but adds the transfer move (snapshots become agent input) that neither the header nor lines 4-6 hold; not doctrine restatement, design commentary or a koan of the header.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A retitled slide re-earns its bullets against the new header.
rules_evaluated.evidence: git log -p: last commit changed '## Talk to customers every week, toward an outcome' to '## Great research can still miss the outcome' (b758b28b), so the trigger fired; covered header and read: it promises the research-without-outcome problem. Line 4 states it, line 6 gives her four-clause answer (the remedy to that problem, not an inherited bullet answering the old header), line 8 the snapshot hand-off. The definition is also quoted on the-product-trio (Day 1), but that is not the neighbouring slide (neighbours are customers-before-agents and what-they-did-not-what-they-say) and the maintainer block declares the paraphrase deliberate.

notes: Single-chunk slide file. Rule 10 verified by include line in the host lecture; composed-deck rendering not re-measured. Three accept-note-bearing maintainer lines (STATUS, two source stamps); none cover a passage a rule would catch.
